# Sprinter Video Frame — PAL-Family Timing Generated by an FPGA

The Peters Plus Sprinter (Спринтер, final model 2000, Sp2000 board) generates its video from a **42 MHz master clock** inside an Altera ACEX EP1K30 FPGA. The result is a **PAL-family frame** — 15.625 kHz line rate, **312 lines at 50.08 Hz** (or 320 lines at ~48.8 Hz) — deliberately matched to the Spectrum/Pentagon cadence so that ZX software keeps its tempo. This is the opposite of the ZX Spectrum Next's VGA-derived timings: the Sprinter is a 50 Hz machine with PC-style *modes*, not a PC-style *sync*.

> [!NOTE]
> This article covers the **video frame timing** of the Sprinter. For the hardware platform (CPU, RAM, I/O, ISA bus), see [sprinter.md](../../02_hardware/newgen/sprinter.md); for the firmware layer (PLD configurations, BIOS, DSS), see [sprinter_firmware.md](../../02_hardware/newgen/sprinter_firmware.md).

---

## Frame Parameters (Sprinter Sp2000)

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Peters Plus Sprinter Frame Timing (Sp2000, ZX configuration)  │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Master clock:            42.000 MHz (FPGA video section)      │
│  Pixel clock:             7 MHz (320-wide modes)               │
│                           14 MHz (640-wide modes)              │
│  Line rate:               15.625 kHz (56 squares × 8 px @7MHz) │
│                                                                │
│  Frame:                    312 lines  → 50.08 Hz   (default)   │
│                            320 lines  → 48.83 Hz  (option)     │
│  Visible area:            40 × 32 squares of 8×8 px            │
│  Full grid:               56 × 39/40 squares (incl. border,    │
│                            blanking and sync)                  │
│                                                                │
│  ZX display:              256×192 + attributes (ZX-40 mode)    │
│  Graphics modes:          320×256×256, 640×256×16 (per cell)   │
│                                                                │
│  T-states per frame @ 3.5 MHz:                                 │
│            312 lines:  69,888  (= Pentagon 128, exactly)       │
│            320 lines:  71,680                                 │
│  @ 21 MHz turbo:         419,328 / 430,080                     │
│                                                                │
│  INT source:              FPGA vertical sync                   │
│  INT position:            selectable: Scorpion / Pentagon /    │
│                            Spectrum (BIOS FN_SINC #F2)         │
│  Contention:              None (dedicated VRAM bus)            │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The numbers are not a coincidence: **224 T-states per line × 312 lines = 69,888 T-states**, the exact Pentagon 128 frame. The 42 MHz clock divides down as `42 ÷ 3 = 14 MHz`, `14 ÷ 2 = 7 MHz` pixel clock, `7 ÷ 8` for the dot-within-square counter, `÷ 56` for the horizontal square counter — giving a 64 µs (15.625 kHz) line and a FLASH divider of 32 frames.

---

## Why the Timing Is Pentagon-Like

The Sprinter's ZX-Spectrum+AY configuration is a **software compatibility target implemented in FPGA**, and its timing was chosen to match the clones the Russian software library was written for:

1. **No contention by construction** — video RAM is a separate chip on its own bus; the FPGA reads it on the video side while the CPU does anything it likes. Like the Pentagon (and unlike the 48K), there are no ULA wait states.
2. **Pentagon frame length** — 69,888 T-states at 3.5 MHz means every frame-counted delay, every music player tempo and every interrupt-driven effect behaves as on a Pentagon 128.
3. **Selectable INT line** — different clones assert INT at different scanlines; the community BIOS (3.05+) exposes the choice (Scorpion / Pentagon / Spectrum / CMOS-saved) in Setup and via BIOS function `FN_SINC` (`#F2`), applied live. A cold start with empty CMOS defaults to the Pentagon INT.
4. **320-line option** — the vertical counter can produce 320 lines per frame (~48.83 Hz, "49 Hz" in Setup) instead of 312, trading frame rate for a taller border grid.

---

## The Screen Grid and the Border

The whole frame is a grid of **56 × 39/40 squares**; only **40 × 32** are the visible ZX screen. The remaining squares cover the border, blanking and sync regions — but they are *addressable*: the designer's manual notes that border squares **can** carry image, just "not recommended, as not all televisions can display this area". The left/top border maps to squares `a = 55` and `b = 38(39)` (wrapped), so border effects are possible but hardware-dependent on the display.

Each square carries its own mode bytes in video RAM (two switchable **mode pages**, selected by bit 0 of port `#C9` RGMOD), which is why ZX-40, ZX-80 text, 320×256×256 and 640×256×16 can coexist on one screen. The palette is RAM-based (RGB triplets in VRAM); in ZX mode the palette address is `attribute (8) + pixel (1) + FLASH (1)` — a 10-bit indirection that reproduces the full 8×2-with-blink Spectrum display without ULA silicon.

---

## INT Timing and ISR Implications

- **Frequency**: 50.08 Hz in the 312-line mode — for a 48K/Pentagon program, tempo is **unchanged**. In the 320-line mode (48.83 Hz) everything frame-counted runs ~2.5% fast.
- **Duration/position**: one scanline's worth; the exact scanline is the selectable INT mode above.
- **Turbo ISRs**: at 21 MHz the frame budget is ~419,328 T-states — 6× a Pentagon frame — but the DRAM wait states and the 7 MHz-bound copy accelerator set the real-world speedup closer to 3–4× for memory-heavy code (code in the 64 KB fast RAM runs without waits).

```
ISR budget comparison (per frame):
  Pentagon 128 @ 3.5 MHz:   69,888 T
  Sprinter ZX  @ 3.5 MHz:   69,888 T   (identical by design)
  Sprinter ZX  @ 21 MHz:  ~419,328 T   (turbo; waits on main DRAM)
```

> [!WARNING]
> Software that measures wall-clock by counting frames still works — but software written for the **320-line option** (48.83 Hz) drifts ~2.5%. Always read the sync mode (BIOS `FN_SINC` / CMOS) if timing accuracy matters, and remember there is **no floating bus and no contention** to race against: effects built on 48K contention timing simply don't apply.

## Detecting Sprinter at Runtime

The page registers are readable, giving a clean probe (full discussion in [sprinter.md §Detecting a Sprinter](../../02_hardware/newgen/sprinter.md)):

```z80
detect_sprinter:
        in   a, (#E2)          ; PAGE3 register is readable
        ld   (saved_page), a
        ld   a, #80            ; page 128 — beyond any 128K clone
        out  (#E2), a
        in   a, (#E2)
        cp   #80
        jr   nz, .not_sprinter
        ld   a, (saved_page)
        out  (#E2), a
        scf                    ; carry = Sprinter
        ret
.not_sprinter:
        ld   a, (saved_page)
        out  (#E2), a
        or   a
        ret
```

Most Sprinter-native software is built specifically for the machine rather than probing at runtime; the probe matters for cross-platform ZX software choosing a timing path.

---

## Sprinter Software Compatibility

| Software type | Compatibility |
|---|---|
| Pure CPU code (algorithms, math, data processing) | **Excellent** — up to 6× the T-state budget in turbo |
| Frame-counted music players | **Good** — 312-line mode matches the Pentagon's 50.08 Hz exactly |
| Graphics rendering to the ZX screen | **Good** — same layout, no contention, palette indirection |
| Race-the-beam multicolor effects | **Broken** — the raster is FPGA-generated; no ULA-style contention interplay |
| Cycle-exact Pentagon demos | **Partial** — no contention or floating bus; INT line selectable but raster racing differs |
| TR-DOS software | **Good** — TR-DOS ROM available from flash; DSS reads TR-DOS disks |
| Tape loaders | **N/A** — no tape interface |

The Sprinter is best understood as a **Pentagon-timed 50 Hz machine with PC-style video modes** — not as a PC-timed machine that happens to run Spectrum software.
